newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes up with WTI, ANS deal done.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes up with WTI, ANS deal done.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices rose late Thursday with March West Texas Intermediate (WTI), traders said, while the Alaskan crude market held steady after a deal got done Wednesday at $1.45 under March.
The Wednesday deal was the same price as a Jan. 17 sale.
Trade was otherwise thin as most players attended the West Coast Crude Oil Conference Thursday and Friday.

Heavy crude markets were also quiet because of the absense of players. But earlier this week, heavy became a stronger alternative to ANS after 40,000 barrels came into the market following a force majeure by Tosco.
With heavy crude prices expected to drop below their current $17.25 range, refiners were looking at ways to run heavies instead of light grades.
Traders said discounts remained 50 to 25 cents under postings. Texaco on Tuesday lowered their posted prices 50 cents and Wednesday Unocal dropped their posting the same amount.
Lower postings pulled down the average price for Kern River about five cnets from Tuesday to $17.25/17.50 cents.
